chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Mansur ibn al-Abbas, from Shu'ayb ibn Janah, from Matar, the freed slave of Ma'n, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

There are three things wherein lies rest for the believer: a spacious house that conceals his private affairs and the wretchedness of his condition from the people; a righteous wife who supports him in the affairs of this world and the Hereafter; and a daughter whom he sends away either by death or by marriage.

key_terms.تَزْوِيجٌ: marriage — the formal conclusion of the father's guardianship and his responsibility to provide
key_terms.رَاحَةٌ: rest, comfort, relief — not mere physical ease but a comprehensive tranquility of life
key_terms.صَالِحَةٌ: righteous, virtuous — a woman of good character and piety who is a genuine helpmeet
key_terms.عَوْرَةٌ: private matters, vulnerabilities, or shameful conditions that one wishes to conceal from others

ai.seo_question: What are the three things that bring rest and comfort to a believer according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) identifies three blessings that bring genuine comfort to a believing man: a spacious home that preserves his dignity and privacy, a virtuous wife who is a true partner in worldly and spiritual life, and a daughter whose departure — whether through death or marriage — relieves the father of his guardianship responsibility. This hadith reflects the social and familial context of early Islamic society, where home privacy, marital partnership, and the resolution of the daughter's dependent status were key concerns for a believing household.
word_analysis: he sends her out/disposes of her

en.hubeali:
Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moalla Bin Muhammad, from Mansour Bin Al Abbas, from Shuayb Bin Janah, from Matar, a slave of Ma’an, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘There are three wherein is rest for the Believer – a spacious house veiling his privacy and the evilness of his state from the people, and a righteous woman who supports him upon the affairs of the world and the Hereafter, and a daughter whom he brings out either due to death or her marriage’.
en.sarwar: 6. Al-FIusayn ibn Muhammad has narrated from Mu’alla’ ibn Muhammad from Mansur ibn al-‘Abbas from Shu’ayb ibn Junah from Matar Mawla’ Ma‘n who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

Three issues provide comfort for a believing person: a spacious house which provides privacy and in bad condition keeps him out of the sight of people, a virtuous wife who helps him in his worldly affairs and those of the life hereafter and a daughter whom he escorts out of the house on her death or on her wedding.’”
